# P14 eng10 stopping and mixed Range observations

These 27 small authored inputs and their recorded results come unchanged from
the eng10 delivery at `~/codex-runs/excel-results-eng10`. Each retained condition
has one trial in a fresh owned Excel process, Excel 16.0.20527.20088, Manual,
events off and MTC off. Every input starts from verified stored values. The two
Rebuild or Range commands are separate observations. There is no new Excel execution here.

`stopping-observations.jsonl` retains the original result objects with their
source result and session receipt hashes. `sha256.json` binds these records and
the exact input packages. The original delivery retains all receipts, raw results,
source scripts, saved workbooks, omissions and failed attempts. An independent
eng14 audit verified all 6,328 delivery files, all 149 qualified trial chains,
their distinct process identities and calculation settings, and every repeated
condition's final-value agreement. There were 118 observed conditions, including
the two historical controls; two requested conditions were unrun. Most conditions
have one trial, so repeatability is not established for them.

The Boolean controls put a NOT self-reference beside a numeric self-reference
incrementing by 0.125 and a downstream `+1` reader. Values immediately below,
equal to and above MaxChange 1 distinguish logical output changes from numeric
stopping samples. A changing-error self-reference without a numeric peer ends
with #N/A on its first command at MaxChange zero and MaxIterations 2 or 5; the
second command gives #DIV/0!. Adding the numeric peer keeps it running.
The numeric-only zero-threshold and equality controls retain strict comparison.

The stopping HostSession regression checks 180 final-value comparisons at unlimited
and one-evaluation budgets. Seeds remain file caches before calculation. Iterative
results still use the existing uncertified publication boundary, and no SliceV1
read certificate is claimed. Intermediate caches, general SCC execution counts,
cyclic Range execution and new observer trials remain separate questions.

`range-observations.jsonl` adds 12 exact mixed-scope inputs and recorded result
objects, with the same source-result and receipt hashes. A1=B1+1, B1=A1+1,
C1=A1+1, D1=2+2 and E1=C1+1 start from zero or asymmetric stored values.
Range A1:D1 and A1:E1 retain cyclic/read-dependent seeds while D1 computes 4,
at MaxIterations 1, 2 and 5. Each condition has one fresh-process trial and two
commands. The test compares 240 display slots at two DNA budgets: 48 independently
evaluated D1 results and 192 retained cache slots. Of those retained slots, 168
are selected unresolved targets and 24 are outside the scope. They remain nonpasses.

DNA admits the Manual scalar mixed request, emits `TargetsRefused` with owner
dc-hsa5.11, and completes as Incomplete with separate calculated/refused counts.
The cyclic targets and conservative graph-reader closure keep their previous
results, calculation identities and unmet requirements. Value and shape reads
cannot consume a selected unresolved cyclic target as an ordinary current result.
An independent result has a producing invocation and certificate for this command,
while Manual StillRequired retains its next-workbook obligation. Warm-cache,
cancellation, supersession and worker serialization controls exercise this DNA
lifecycle; they are not additional Excel observations. Automatic mixed requests,
tables, callbacks, multi-cell arrays/spills and newly discovered cycles retain
typed refusals. No cyclic target is claimed as calculated, and SCC execution
counts and mid-cycle cache observations remain open.

A typed refusal during the admitted mixed command stops it before replacing a
warm result. A missing outside cache can stop a reader before it reveals its own
self-reference; a later Rebuild must still use that retained seed. The two-budget
control exercises this DNA integrity rule without a new Excel observation.
